guide.description: Use one fictionalized public-relations crisis to compare three meeting scripts—from preparation to a report—without a model key or a real meeting record.
guide.eyebrow: Fictional exercise · no key · no local write

brainstorm.cheat: Remind the team not to amplify unverified details. Explore one response angle at a time, then screen ideas by factual grounding, de-escalation, and speed.
brainstorm.copyReason: The team needs to open a responsible response space before assembling the next 24 hours.
brainstorm.label: Brainstorm together
brainstorm.modeEffect: This script protects divergence, then converges on facts, de-escalation, and speed so the team is not trapped by a fight-or-settle binary.
brainstorm.outcome1: Keep three response paths that can be combined
brainstorm.outcome2: Content owner drafts first assets within two hours
brainstorm.outcome3: Team screens by facts, de-escalation, and speed
brainstorm.question: Beyond fighting back or settling, what could lower the temperature while preserving room to act?
brainstorm.rawRequest: Use a fictional exercise in which Sun posts publicly and JT's team must respond. Brainstorm a 24-hour plan without amplifying unverified details.
brainstorm.readinessSummary: The communications challenge is clear; priority audiences, publishable facts, and selection criteria still need boundaries.
brainstorm.reason: Breaking the binary reveals combinable moves such as verification, mediated contact, and staged communication.
brainstorm.report:
# 24-hour response brainstorm

## Candidate paths
- Verify facts before responding
- Open a third-party channel
- Publish in clear stages

## Next step
Combine actions by factual grounding, de-escalation, and speed.
brainstorm.title: 24-hour response brainstorm

decision.cheat: Confirm verifiable facts, the deadline, and the decision owner. Test the best and worst cases for fighting back and settling, check a third path, then restate the choice, owner, and reporting point.
decision.copyReason: The team needs a clear choice inside a high-pressure, low-tolerance response window.
decision.expansion1: Clarify publicly with an evidence bar
decision.label: Align on a decision
decision.modeEffect: This script exposes the situation and loss, options, best and worst cases, decision authority, and deadline before the room makes the call.
decision.outcome1: Verify facts first and preserve a settlement channel
decision.outcome2: PR lead delivers the execution list within two hours
decision.outcome3: Review sentiment every four hours and brief JT
decision.question: If the team cannot agree, who has enough authority to make the final call before the deadline?
decision.rawRequest: Use a fictional exercise in which Sun posts publicly and JT's PR team has one hour to choose a firm response, reconciliation, or a third option, then brief JT.
decision.readinessSummary: The deadline and two main options are known; actual impact, a third option, risk tolerance, and final authority remain incomplete.
decision.reason: Under time pressure and low tolerance for error, named authority prevents analysis from ending without a decision.
decision.report:
# JT public-response decision

## Tradeoff
Verify what can be proven, avoid escalating publicly for now, and preserve a reconciliation channel.

## Action
PR lead delivers the message, task list, and owners within two hours.

## Follow-up
Review sentiment every four hours and brief JT.
decision.title: JT public-response decision

retro.cheat: Open with shared facts such as timestamps, published copy, and sentiment measures. Separate cause from blame, compare expected with actual, then close on owned improvements.
retro.copyReason: The team needs to understand why the first response did not de-escalate the situation and agree on improvements.
retro.label: Reflect and improve
retro.modeEffect: This script separates the timeline and verifiable facts from interpretation, compares expected with actual, then converts learning into owned response improvements.
retro.objective: Learn why the first response did not de-escalate
retro.outcome2: Response owner maintains one shared Q&A
retro.outcome3: Measure impact four hours after the next response
retro.question: Which verifiable measures show that discussion did not cool after the first response?
retro.rawRequest: Review the first response in this fictional crisis exercise, learn why discussion kept escalating, and decide what to change next.
retro.readinessSummary: The first actions are known; the shared timeline, expected measures, actual change, and follow-up ownership still need separation.
retro.reason: Aligning on observable change keeps the retro from becoming subjective blame about wording or individuals.
retro.report:
# First-response retro

## Finding
The response lagged behind the spread and missed the public's central questions.

## Improvement
Use a one-hour fact-verification checklist and one shared Q&A.

## Owner
The response owner measures impact four hours after the next release.
retro.title: First-response crisis retro
